S7 Class for Marginal Break-Point Terms

Source: R/marginal.R
MarginalBreakTerm.Rd

The subclass of structural_term() holding break-points that vary by group as latent variables integrated out of the likelihood. jump(), seg() and jseg() construct it when given marginal = TRUE together with a psi ~ random(~ 1 | g) subformula.

Its contribution is a likelihood, not a predictor, so it implements term_loglik() and the prior over the positions is part of that likelihood itself. term_penalties() declares nothing, and the prior's parameters are estimated by plain maximum likelihood.

Usage

MarginalBreakTerm(
  label = character(0),
  hyper = list(),
  grid = list(),
  values = list(),
  min_ratio = numeric(0),
  search = character(0),
  ids = character(0),
  blueprint = list(),
  kind = character(0),
  var = NULL,
  npsi = integer(0),
  linear = logical(0),
  group = NULL,
  prior = NULL,
  spec = list()
)

Arguments

label

A character string prefixed to the term's coefficient names when non-empty, and used as the title of plot() and the tag of print(). The empty string "" means no label.

hyper

The hyperparameters of the term's penalty that the caller held, as a named list keyed by the penalty's names. Empty, the default, means every one of them is estimated. See term_hyper().

grid

How many values a path visits for each of the term's hyperparameters, as a named list of single whole numbers. Empty, the default, leaves the number to the fitting layer. See term_grid().

values

The values a path visits, for each hyperparameter the caller wrote out, as a named list of numeric vectors. Empty, the default, has the path build them. See term_values().

min_ratio

How far down the path over the size of the kink reaches, as a fraction of the value that empties the block: one number in \((0, 1)\), or numeric(0) for the fitting layer's own. See term_path_min().

search

How the term's own hyperparameters are covered when it has more than one carrying a kink: "grid" for every combination of them, "cyclic" for one at a time, or character(0) for the default. See term_search().

ids

Which of the term's hyperparameters are shared with those of other terms, and under what label: a character vector named by the term's own hyperparameters, or character(0) for none. The terms carrying the same label for the same hyperparameter estimate one value. See term_ids().

blueprint

A named list recording the number of rows, the covariate, the rows of each group and the group labels, empty until term_build() fills it.

kind

One of "jump", "seg" or "jseg".

var

The covariate expression, unevaluated.

npsi

The number of break-points per group, an integer between 1 and 8 for "jump" and exactly 1 for the other two.

linear

Whether the term carries the linear effect as its own parameter, beta. It is FALSE for "jump".

group

The grouping expression, from the break-point's random() subformula.

prior

The latent's distribution: NULL for the Gaussian, or a distributions7 object with its location held at zero.

spec

A named list of the resolved construction settings.

Value

An S7 object of class MarginalBreakTerm, inheriting from structural_term() and model_term(), with the properties listed above beside the inherited ones.

Properties

The class defines the properties kind, var, npsi, linear, group, prior and spec, and inherits the others from structural_term() and model_term(), among them blueprint.

kind is "jump", "seg" or "jseg"; var is the covariate expression; npsi is the number of break-points per group; linear records whether the term carries the linear effect as a parameter of its own. It is TRUE for seg() and jseg() unless linear = FALSE was given, and FALSE for jump().

group is the grouping expression, taken from the break-point's random() subformula. prior is the distribution of the latent positions: NULL for the Gaussian, or a distributions7 object where random(distrib = ) names one. The location of that distribution must be fixed at zero, since psi1.mean carries the position.

spec holds the resolved construction settings. blueprint is inherited from structural_term() and holds the grouping and the covariate that term_build() records.

Parameters

The parameters are numbered, one set per break-point. A step term with one break-point has psi1.mean, psi1.sd and delta1, where psi1.mean is the mean of the positions in the population, psi1.sd is their standard deviation between groups (estimated through a log link) and delta1 is the change of level. A seg() term has beta for the linear effect, psi1.mean, psi1.sd and gamma1 for the change of slope. A jseg() term has beta, psi1.mean, psi1.sd, gamma1 and delta1.

Number of break-points

A step term takes at most eight break-points per group. The forward recursion of the step kind costs \(n K 2^K\) operations for \(n\) observations and \(K\) break-points. The fitting layer reads a posterior over the \(2^K\) side patterns and evaluates the family once per pattern, and the number of patterns therefore limits \(K\). The continuous kinds take one break-point, because a product quadrature over several would need a node set whose size grows as a power of their number.

See also

jump(), seg() and jseg() for the constructors; term_loglik() for the likelihood; term_latent() for the posterior positions.

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(id = rep(1:3, each = 8), x = rep(1:8, 3))
dd$y <- rnorm(24, 2 * (dd$x >= 4.5), 0.4)

tm <- term_build(jump(x, psi ~ random(~ 1 | id), marginal = TRUE), dd)
S7::S7_inherits(tm, MarginalBreakTerm)
#> [1] TRUE
c(kind = tm@kind, npsi = tm@npsi, linear = tm@linear)
#>    kind    npsi  linear 
#>  "jump"     "1" "FALSE" 

# Numbered parameters: the prior's location and scale, and the change.
term_params(tm)
#> [1] "psi1.mean" "psi1.sd"   "delta1"   
vapply(term_links(tm), function(l) l@link_name, character(1))
#>  psi1.mean    psi1.sd     delta1 
#> "identity"      "log" "identity" 

# The prior is part of the likelihood, so nothing is declared penalized.
length(term_penalties(tm))
#> [1] 0

# A continuous kind adds the linear effect and the change of slope.
term_params(term_build(seg(x, psi ~ random(~ 1 | id), marginal = TRUE), dd))
#> [1] "beta"      "psi1.mean" "psi1.sd"   "gamma1"
